title: [PDF] Supervisory Stress Test Documentation Credit Risk Models
summary: The Federal Reserve published technical documentation detailing the credit risk models it intends to use in the 2026 Supervisory Stress Test, covering Corporate, Commercial Real Estate, First Lien Mortgage, Home Equity, Credit Card, Auto, and Other Retail Models. The document was revised in January 2026 to provide additional transparency on model coefficients and technical corrections. This is granular regulatory methodology documentation with no direct relevance to market structure or macro catalysts for trading purposes.
key_points: Document covers credit risk models for 2026 Supervisory Stress Test including Corporate, CRE, First Lien Mortgage, Home Equity, Credit Card, Auto, and Other Retail categories
January 2026 revision added transparency on coefficients used in proposed credit risk models and made technical corrections
Corporate Model section includes statement of purpose, model overview, and ad-hoc adjustments (starting page 7)
Commercial Real Estate Model section details PD Model regression specification and LGD Model discount factor regression (pages 47-115)
Revisions clarify omitted loan types, property types, and proximity to maturity categories in CRE models
Credit Card Model includes Bank Card PD Model and Charge Card PD Model with detailed variable category specifications (pages 386-447)
why_it_matters: This document provides the technical methodology behind the Fed's 2026 bank stress tests. While important for bank regulatory compliance and capital planning, it does not contain actionable market intelligence on trading dynamics, market plumbing, or current macro catalysts. It is technical model documentation aimed at regulated institutions, not market participants seeking tradeable signals.
